name: Northwest Ridge Integral
text: [approach] Leave the car on the highway's south shoulder, east of the Hermit lot and short of the avalanche snowshed.

name: North Face Couloir
text: [overview] Cross the creek from the logging road at Centre Creek and ascend the gully (ideally snow-filled) to the basin with a pocket glacier beneath the Spires.
[overview] Get over a bergschrund that is tricky, then go up Priest-Coupe, the couloir lying between Rexford and the South Nesakwatch Spire.

[overview] Roughly 80 m short of its top, break left up a narrow slot or chimney for one pitch, then go left across ice bulges, following a snow runnel that opens out, to join the NE ridge high up, with 70 m left to the summit.
[detailed_rack] a picket or two;
[approach] Reach the Centre Creek logging road and cross the creek, then follow the gully, which may be snow-filled, into the basin above the pocket glacier below the Nesakwatch Spires.
[approach] Cross the bergschrund and climb the couloir between Rexford and South Nesakwatch Spire.

name: Priest-Coupe (NE Couloir)
text: [overview] Bergschrunds pose the main technical problem, calling for brief mixed or vertical-snow moves to get over them.
[overview] Gear may be placeable in the couloir walls, though big moats can develop later in the season.
[overview] Snow and ice can fall from the walls overhead.

name: West Ridge
text: [approach] The ridge is mainly scrambling with a few fifth-class sections, and no glacier travel is needed.
[descent_text] It alternates between snow and rock, with krummholz to push through and a few short rappels, and it ends in a basin on the Centre Creek side, well away from the Nesakwatch approach.

name: Emperor Ridge
text: [overview] A serious, committing ridge whose difficulty depends heavily on the state of the snow gargoyles;
[overview] if the snow is bad, retreat is the only option.
[detailed_rack] Some ice and snow gear plus a modest rock rack.

name: Patterson Couloir
text: [overview] It could give a fast way toward the foot of the Kain Face in spring, once deep snow covers the brush, the Dome's rocks are plastered in place and avalanches have scoured the couloir.

name: Wishbone Arete
text: [description] The Wishbone is a long ridge of loose rock, snow and ice;

name: Coldwell Creek Couloir
text: [overview] Cross to the foot of the narrow couloir and climb it, up to about 45 degrees at its steepest, until it opens into a wider snow slope at the saddle by Pump Peak.
[detailed_rack] Pickets or screws only for roping up.

name: Not-so-grand Sorta-central (NS) Couloir
text: [overview] A steep snow gully with several mixed steps, a fun outing when snow is thin;
[overview] it was climbed in about 40 cm of snow.
[overview] P1 (M4-) opens with an M3 bouldery step, then steep snow and then a second, longer bouldery step at M4-, and belays at a tree on the right.
[overview] P2 (M2) climbs a steep snow ramp, ending at a belay from pitons on the left side.
[approach] The hut itself is a couple of hours from the summer parking, longer in deep snow.

[descent_text] Below the last of the face stations, scree and ledges lead to slab or snow at the base of a dihedral, then two more rappels or 4th-class downclimbing reach the scree trail back to the Uto-Sir Donald col.

name: West Ridge
text: [approach] Walk up from the Hermit parking area to Hermit Meadows, then follow cairns and a faint beaten path through meadows and past waterfalls to a low point on the west ridge above the Tupper glacier, the Tupper shoulder.

name: Southwest Face
text: [beta] Reach a snow ridge and then the crux wall of small ledges below the summit block;
[hazards] Hard snow ridge.
[obj_haz] Hard old snow patches
[gear] Crampons for the snow ridge.
[descent_text] Descend the same route, downclimbing the crux wall carefully, then glissade or plunge-step snow patches and descend the long loose rubble of the lower gully.
[turnaround] Turn back if snow on the ridge is too hard to cross safely or if water and daylight are running low in the heat.
[pitch_detail] Steep, very loose rubble slopes to a snow ridge..

name: Northeast Spur (PD+)
text: [overview] Difficulties are mainly on the snow apron at 45 degrees below the rock, where many lines are possible;

name: Massey's
text: [overview] Once the first ice section ends the angle relents: either belay and bring up the second, or continue through more ice to a snowfield, then go left around it and anchor on good ice (one 70 m rope covers all this in a single pitch).

grade: 5.0 V16 WI1 M1 C0 Easy Snow

name: North Face
text: [overview] A steep band at the base leads to a large low-angle shield of heather or snow, with another steep band near the top.
[overview] Climbed in summer (solo), when it is heathery with poor climbing, and in winter, when it has two distinct cruxes around M4 separated by frozen heather and steep snow that is not hard.
[detailed_rack] Some gear helps in winter: pieces that can be driven into frozen heather or a crack filled with snow and ice without pulling out, such as hexes, tri-cams and spectres.

name: North Nesakwatch Spire - Nesakwatch Notch (NE Buttress)
text: [overview] Conditions are tricky: snow must fill the notch, after which the climbing is rock.
[overview] Reach it from Centre Creek by crossing the stream and ascending a snow gully to the basin, as on Rexford's north face.
[overview] go up snow beneath the chockstone that stands alone, then downclimb one pitch beyond, under the N face.

text: [overview] From the bottom of the NW face, a ramp slanting across (snow and rock, 4th class) leads up to the west ridge beneath its 5.7 crack pitch, then stay on the ridge to the summit.

name: Arete Du Phalanx (Phalanx South Arete)
text: [overview] The initial half is mostly 3rd/4th class, snow or rock, ending at a prominent spire: sling it, then either rappel or downclimb, and cross steep snow rightward.
[overview] Beyond, the narrow aesthetic arete (low 5th) can be bypassed by an easier traverse, up and to the right across steep snow.
[overview] The final ridge brings further steep snow plus easy mixed ground.

text: [overview] Spring ascents will find the cracks iced and snowy, so consider an ice axe;
[approach] From the Sphinx (Burton) Hut on the southeast side of Garibaldi Lake, climb glaciated terrain to the ridge.

name: Lentils or TVP, eh?
text: [descent_text] From the summit, downclimb east along the ridge to slings for a short rappel onto broken ground, from which the Crack of Noon route or a snow descent can be reached.

name: Lee/Hinkkala North West Face Route - Rugged Mountain
text: [overview] The lower third is moderate hard snow with small ice patches and some outcrops of rock, leading to a chimney with good ice and a grade 3 exit.

[overview] About 4-5 long pitches reach a rightward-trending ramp, followed by steep snice pitches with a rock alcove belay, a steep snow ramp, and a brief gully with exposure before steep snow to the summit.
[overview] Descend by a v-thread rappel, the East ridge, and three 60 m rappels to the glacier.
[detailed_rack] Rack used: 2 pickets, 1 fluke or deadman, 7 screws (2 x 13, 4 x 16, 1 x 22), cams .3 to #2, 6 nuts, 6 pins, bird beak, bulldog, 2 tricams, plus 7 alpine quickdraws and 4 screamers.

text: [overview] A snow ramp running diagonally alongside the north buttress leads to the gap behind the conspicuous gendarme.
[approach] Follow the Slesse Memorial Trail to the Propeller Cairn, then traverse south across snowpatches to the Labour Day Horn buttress.
[approach] A long diagonal snow ramp runs beside the north buttress up to a notch behind the prominent gendarme, which is the start of the pillar.

name: Flight 810 Buttress
text: [descent_text] Depending on the snow, the couloir can be a continuous downclimb on snow or a series of rappels over polished rock with weak anchors.

text: [approach] Continue north over glacier-polished slabs, losing a little height toward a wooded ridge, and scramble a short gully (third to fourth class, often damp) to a notch in it.
